title: Juniper and the Current
premise: Rafael Thackeray, a disgraced mountain guide hiding in the border town of Juniper's Landing, pulls a sealed chest from the river and finds it stamped with the seal of Vessia—a nation erased from maps twenty years ago. Inside are documents proving the current government's concession permits were forged from stolen Vessian land grants, and a name Rafael recognizes: the man who betrayed them both. Hunted by a magistrate who wants the chest destroyed and shadowed by a Vessian exile who wants it published, Rafael must guide a small party across the range before the first snows close the passes and before the permits expire, making the fraud permanent. At the summit pass, Rafael chooses justice over safety, surrendering the documents to the exiles' courier at the cost of their own escape route—and returns not as a ghost, but as a witness.
about_author: Noor Sandoval is a former trail crew lead who spent six seasons mapping high passes across three borders before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the maps forgot, from a cabin they refuse to give exact coordinates for.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Rafael. Working a low-water season on the Serrano River, Rafael hooks something heavy: an iron chest stamped with the Vessian seal. The emotional beat is dread disguised as curiosity—Rafael knows exactly what that seal means and what it cost them once.

chapters.title: A Debt with Teeth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback threads reveal the debt: money owed to the ferryman Osric for smuggling Rafael across the border two years ago. Rafael pawns nothing, tells no one, but can't stop opening the chest at night. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Reads Ciphers
chapters.summary: Introduce Mirela Vance, a Vessian exile working as a bookbinder, POV shared through a tense market encounter. She glimpses the seal on Rafael's sleeve-stain and follows him home. Beat: two cautious people recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: What the Chest Contains
chapters.summary: Mirela decodes the documents: land grants proving the republic's mining concessions were built on forged transfers from dissolved Vessia. Rafael's POV; the beat is vertigo—staying invisible was never an option, because someone hid this where only a guide could find it.

chapters.title: Magistrate Corven
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. The magistrate learns a chest surfaced and quietly posts watchers in Juniper's Landing. We see his cold arithmetic: if the permits expire unchallenged, the theft becomes law. Beat: menace without violence—yet.

chapters.title: Osric Calls It In
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Osric demands repayment now, in full, or he sells word of the chest to Corven's men. Rafael has eleven days and no money. Beat: the walls closing in, duty and debt colliding.

chapters.title: The Permit Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. She confirms the concessions expire at season's end; after that, the forged titles are uncontestable. The documents must reach the Vessian exile council over the range before snowfall. Beat: hope arriving with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Two Countries That Want Me Gone
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, reflective. Why Rafael was blacklisted: blamed for a client's death on the Vessian side of the range—a death Rafael has never been able to explain or forgive. Beat: shame laid bare, setting up the memory theme.

chapters.title: Hiring the Impossible Party
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Rafael recruits a small crossing party: Osric (as payment-in-kind), Mirela, and young ferry-hand Tam who idolizes Rafael. Beat: reluctant fellowship forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: Corven corners Rafael privately: surrender the chest, receive a clean passport and debt forgiveness. Rafael refuses, and Corven marks them. Beat: love against duty begins—Rafael's duty to truth outweighing survival.

chapters.title: Last Market Day
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Quiet interlude: she and Rafael trade histories over cheap wine; a fragile tenderness takes root neither will name. Beat: warmth banked against the cold to come.

chapters.title: The Watcher on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. He spots Corven's agent tailing the party and, panicking, leads them astray—buying hours but burning their anonymity. Beat: first bloodless skirmish, first real consequence.

chapters.title: Up the Serrano Gorge
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The climb begins; Rafael's old mastery returns and the party starts to trust them. A rockfall nearly kills Tam. Beat: competence as redemption, fear as glue.

chapters.title: The Burned Village
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. They camp in ruins of a Vessian settlement razed during annexation; she names the dead from memory while Rafael listens. Beat: grief made communal, memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Osric's Bargain Shifts
chapters.summary: Osric's POV. Corven's men reached him by runner: betray the party at the high camp and his debt vanishes twice over. He says nothing yet. Beat: treachery germinating inside a likeable man.

chapters.title: Whiteout at Windrow Col
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. An early storm traps them; Rafael navigates by compass and memory of a route no map shows. Beat: the compass—gift from the dead client—becomes symbol and burden.

chapters.title: What Happened on the Vessian Side
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, confession scene by firelight. The truth of the client's death: Corven ordered the route changed and let Rafael carry the blame. Beat: rage replacing shame; the blacklisting reframed as design.

chapters.title: The High Camp Split
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Storm damage forces a choice: one fast group carries the documents, one slower group shelters. Mirela insists on going fast; Rafael refuses to split. Beat: love against duty, argued openly for the first time.

chapters.title: Corven Ascends
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. He's brought twelve riders up the southern approach, permits expiring in four days, patience gone. Beat: the hunter becoming weather—inevitable, impersonal, closing.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. He discovers Osric's messages to Corven and confronts him privately; Osric, ashamed, wavers but doesn't recant. Beat: loyalty tested in the young, mercy extended to the guilty.

chapters.title: The Glacier Crossing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A day-long traverse of crevassed ice, rope-work, near-loss of the chest into a crevasse—saved by Mirela. Beat: trust forged in rope and fear; the romance becomes undeniable without being spoken.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Silence
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. In a snow cave, she and Rafael finally speak plainly: she lost her family to the annexation, he lost his name to Corven. They admit they're falling in love. Beat: tenderness at altitude, fully earned.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Shelf Camp
chapters.summary: Osric's POV. Cornered by Corven's advance rider, Osric gives up the route—then sabotages the information out of conscience, sending riders onto a dead-end shelf. Beat: betrayal and repentance in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Pass Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They reach Thackeray Pass—the same pass from the fatal expedition—with a day to spare. But Corven's true column is behind them, and the exile council's courier is ahead, unreachable. Beat: triumph shadowed by trap.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Narrows
chapters.summary: Action chapter, ensemble POV rotating. Corven's riders catch them in a canyon; Tam is taken hostage; the chest is seized. Beat: devastating reversal, everything lost in minutes.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV, captive. Corven offers to spare the others if Mirela authenticates the documents as forgeries—his cover story. She refuses. Beat: courage without audience, the theme of justice outside the law embodied.

chapters.title: The Compass Pointing Back
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, escaped downriver with Osric's help. Rafael realizes the compass needle pulls toward the dead client's cache—a hidden second set of originals. Beat: memory literally guiding the way home.

chapters.title: The Cache Under the Cairn
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Digging beneath the memorial cairn, Rafael finds the client's own copies and a letter absolving Rafael by name. Beat: catharsis—the past hands back the future.

chapters.title: Raising the Valley
chapters.summary: Osric's POV. He spends every favor he owns: ferrymen, shepherds, the exile network. By dawn, thirty civilians stand between Corven's riders and the pass. Beat: ordinary people choosing justice over obedience.

chapters.title: Standoff at Thackeray Pass
chapters.summary: Climax begins, Rafael's POV. Corven demands the documents; Rafael produces the letter clearing their name and the original grants, witnessed by the crowd. Corven orders his riders forward; some refuse. Beat: authority cracking under witness.

chapters.title: The Rider Who Wouldn't
chapters.summary: Sergeant Ilsa Brandt's POV, one of Corven's own. She dismounts, testifies to orders she was given to falsify survey records. Beat: the machine turning on its maker.

chapters.title: Snowfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The first true snow arrives mid-standoff, making retreat the only sane order. Corven, permits expired and witnesses multiplying, withdraws—but promises ruin. Beat: nature as impartial judge; victory incomplete.

chapters.title: What the Courier Carried
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. The exile council's courier, delayed by the storm, finally arrives—and so do copies Mirela mailed weeks earlier from Juniper's Landing. Redundancy saves the truth. Beat: quiet cleverness rewarded; relief after terror.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Osric
chapters.summary: Osric's POV. He confesses his bargain publicly, expecting exile; instead Rafael forgives the debt outright. Beat: mercy as the story's moral center, costly and freely given.

chapters.title: Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Descent through deepening winter, the party transformed—Tam steadier, Mirela and Rafael hand in hand, Rafael's name spoken without flinching. Beat: gentle falling action, wounds acknowledged.

chapters.title: Corven's Last Card
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. Facing inquiry, he attempts to burn the archive in Juniper's Landing; Tam and the ferrymen save it, and Corven is arrested by his own garrison. Beat: the architect buried by his blueprints.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. The tribunal in the valley town hears the documents read aloud; the concessions voided; Vessian families notified. Rafael testifies last, voice steady. Beat: justice achieved through process, not vengeance.

chapters.title: The Name on the Register
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The mountain guild restores Rafael's license; the register lists 'Thackeray, R.—guide, cleared.' Rafael signs the new permit ledger for next season. Beat: identity restored, the blacklist broken.

chapters.title: Juniper in Spring
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Epilogue-adjacent: the chest's contents bound into a public archive Mirela curates; she and Rafael share a house above the ferry landing. Beat: love settled into daily life, memory honored rather than mourned.

chapters.title: The Current Goes On
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Rafael's POV, years later. Rafael guides Tam's first licensed crossing over Thackeray Pass, pauses at the cairn, and lets the river below carry the last of the old weight away. Beat: closure—the current moves, and so do they.
